newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach's SWT orders 30 new trains.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach's SWT orders 30 new trains.

text.p: British transport group Stagecoach Holdings Plc on Tuesday said its subsidiary South West Trains had ordered 30 new trains worth more than 90 million stg.

The electric, four-car trains will be built in Britain by GEC-Alsthom -- a joint venture of Britain's General Electric Co Plc and France's Alcatel Alsthom -- for Porterbrook Leasing Co Ltd and leased to SWT in 1999/2000, Stagecoach said in a statement.
The order, above Stagecoach's franchise commitments, is the first major one for new passenger trains to be completed since privatisation, it said. The trains will replace 30-year-old slam-door stock.
"The order demonstrates Stagecoach's commitment to investment in the rail industry and to improving facilities for passengers," SWT chairman and managing director Brian Cox said in a statement.
"SWT will be announcing a package of measures to bring further passenger benefits over the next few weeks". -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4365
